R170.note: Adds @csrf_protect in the same decorator order already proven on update_profile_note; closes the gap with no other change.

R171.note: Primary fix calls $this->authorize() but OrderRefundController extends nothing (no AuthorizesRequests trait), so every request would hit 'call to undefined method'; the alternative route-middleware+policy fix given in the same write-up would work.

R172.note: Strict [a-zA-Z0-9.-]+ allowlist blocks every cmd.exe metacharacter before batchLine is built; ping/nslookup chain and output handling unchanged for valid input.

R173.note: Recommends org.eclipse.angus:jakarta.mail 2.0.4 / jakarta.mail-api 2.1.0 (verified: that jar contains only jakarta.mail.* classes, no javax.mail.*) alongside code that imports javax.mail.*, which only compiles under the older 1.6.8 artifact also mentioned; also silently adds mail.smtp.starttls.required=true, a new requirement not in the original and not flagged as a compatibility risk with the internal mail server.

R174.note: SVG removed from the storage allowlist (disclosed), content-type resolved via a closed png/jpg map with a generic fallback; matches the stated PNG/JPEG contract.

R175.note: PasswordSignInAsync(TUser,...) throws ArgumentNullException on a null user (documented Identity design - the username-string overload exists precisely to avoid this), but the fix calls it with the possibly-null resolved user before checking for null, so every login attempt against a nonexistent username throws an unhandled exception instead of returning 'Invalid login attempt'; the decoy-hash timing mitigation is unreachable, and this regression isn't disclosed.

R176.note: Cleanly removes the shell via separate exec.Command argument arrays plus allowlist regex; but w.WriteHeader(500) is called after w.Write() on the error path, which Go's net/http ignores (status already sent as 200), so command failures silently return HTTP 200 with partial output instead of the original 500 - not disclosed.

R177.note: Clean argument-array replacement, drops the now-unused fmt import, preserves the exact convert arguments and cmd.Run() return value per the stated contract.

R178.note: Correct parameterized-query technique, but the diff never shows renaming the outer 'Statement sqlStatement = null' declaration to PreparedStatement, so 'preparedStatement' referenced in the updated finally block is out of scope as literally given.

R179.note: GetFullPath + StartsWith(root+separator) correctly closes the Path.Combine absolute-path override without disturbing legitimate relative-path reads.

R180.note: HMAC-signing is a reasonable choice given the batch job is out of scope (disclosed dependency), but entry_data["data"].encode("latin-1") never actually base64-decodes the field the code's own comment calls base64-encoded, so pickle.loads() would fail even once the batch job produces the described format.

R181.note: Allowlist restricts extraCriteria to exactly the 'status' key the route's own comment says is the legitimate use case, closing the ownerId-override authorization bypass without reducing intended functionality.

R182.note: Verified by compiling against golang-jwt/jwt v4 and v5 (v5.2.1/v5.3.1): WithValidMethods takes methods []string, not variadic strings, so jwt.WithValidMethods("RS256","RS384","RS512") fails to compile in every version.

R183.note: redis-py's parameterized .hset(mapping=...) correctly closes the RESP command-injection vector; but the function now returns a {"status":"ok"} dict instead of the original raw socket response bytes, an undisclosed change to the return value.

R184.note: Resolve-then-normalize-then-startsWith is the correct order, and Java's Path.startsWith compares path segments so it isn't vulnerable to a sibling-directory prefix bug; matches the stated contract exactly.

R185.note: Rejecting any URI with a host and any absolute opaque URI, allowing only relative paths, closes the open redirect; the resulting behavior change is the intended fix and is stated openly.

R186.note: Allowlist maps tool names to fixed absolute paths so user input never reaches exec.Command as the program name, plus a leading-dash check on target; output format unchanged.
